definitions.explanation: The tough outer covering of the trunk and branches of a tree. A somewhat technical word used in science, forestry, and writing.

examples.japanese: {樹皮|じゅひ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧はがれて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。

examples.english: Deer have eaten the bark off the trees.

examples.japanese: ⟦{和紙|わし}→和紙：02268_washi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{楮|こうぞ}⟦など→〜など：03095_nado⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{樹皮|じゅひ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{繊維|せんい}→繊維：13857_seni⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{作|つく}られる→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: Washi paper is made from the fibers of the bark of paper mulberry and similar trees.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {樹皮|じゅひ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧はぐ: to strip the bark
- {樹皮|じゅひ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧はがれる: the bark peels off
- {樹皮|じゅひ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{繊維|せんい}→繊維：13857_seni⟧: bark fiber

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{皮|かわ}→皮：02187_kawa⟧: the everyday way to say tree bark
- ⟦{皮|かわ}→皮：02187_kawa⟧: skin, peel, bark in general
